KNIGHT's codebase is organized around three distinct, independently useful
artifacts: a knowledge-graph construction pipeline, a GraphRAG query layer
built on top of it, and an interactive Streamlit application for
KG-grounded neuromorphic co-design. Repository links below are placeholders
pending public release approval.

::: {.software-card}
### KG Construction Pipeline
`kg-builder`

Python package (Typer CLI) that transforms a corpus of scientific PDFs into
a structured, deduplicated knowledge graph. Stages: `save-inputs -> extract ->
merge -> postmerge -> dedupe -> cluster -> embed -> ontology -> check`. Supports
multi-model parallel LLM extraction (vLLM + Ollama backends), fuzzy-matching
deduplication, Louvain clustering, FAISS embedding indices, and OWL ontology
generation with consistency checking. The multimodal extension used by the
Neuromorphic Codesign Agent adds DeepSeek-OCR-2 ingestion plus formula, code,
and SPICE netlist node types with cross-modal edge construction.

::: {.software-card}
### GraphRAG Query Layer
`graphrag` (part of `kg-builder`)

Multi-stage retrieval-and-reasoning engine that queries the constructed KG:
FAISS vector similarity search for entry-node discovery, k-hop BFS graph
traversal to collect a relevant subgraph of triples with provenance, hybrid
reranking by triple coverage and semantic similarity, and role-specific LLM
routing (extractor -> ranker -> reasoner) to synthesize a cited answer. The
codesign-agent variant extends this with GraphSAGE neighborhood sampling,
cross-modal traversal (concept -> formula -> code -> netlist), and query-type-
aware attention weighting, plus a built-in standard-GraphRAG baseline
comparison for every query.

### Streamlit Codesign Application
`streamlit_app_modular.py`

Interactive web application implementing the Neuromorphic Codesign Agent's
online phase: KG search, research analysis (limitations, novelty, evolution
chains), a four-strategy hypothesis engine (limitation-, analogy-, gap-, and
conflict-driven) with embedding-based deduplication and five-dimensional
scoring, three-stage LLM critique and sharpening, six-source constraint
extraction, constrained Python code generation (seven-check validation
loop), and SPICE netlist generation (five-check validation loop with six
post-processing stages) -- with a GraphRAG baseline comparison surfaced
alongside every result.
